selected.assays: skeletal muscle (vastus lateralis biopsy) and serum EV; long, small and circular RNA-seq (abstract; GEO overall_design)
selected.primary_estimand: within-protocol acute exercise response of the skeletal-muscle long-RNA (protein-coding) transcriptome: h3 and h24 post-exercise vs pre, paired within subject, separately for TRAD (n=21) and HITT (n=19); between-protocol difference in that response as secondary
selected.scope_selected: skeletal muscle long-RNA counts only (GSE209880_muscle_long_counts.txt.gz). Serum EV and small/circular RNA streams are out of scope for 'how exercise affects gene expression' and are not analysed here.

factors.subject: PH id, 40 subjects, each sampled at all three muscle time points

selected.inclusion: 40 young adults randomized to TRAD (12M/9F) or HITT (11M/8F) (abstract)
planned_contrasts: TRAD h3 vs pre (abstract: DE 'within ... exercise protocols' at h3)
TRAD vs HITT response at h3 and h24 (abstract: 'between exercise protocols'; exact model not stated)
selected.repeated_measure_unit: subject (pre/h3/h24 biopsies from the same person)
selected.paper_method: not stated in the abstract or GEO record (full text not available)
selected.paper_results: abstract gives no DEG counts or named genes; only that TRAD generally elicited a stronger transcriptional response than HITT, and more consistent protein-coding gene responses to TRAD

decisions.reason: No full text is available; the study map rests on the PubMed abstract and the GEO series summary/overall design only. Both state the threshold |log2FC|>1, FDR<=0.05 and the within- and between-protocol comparisons at h0 (EV only), h3, h24.

checks: GEO summary reproduces the abstract (TRAD n=21 12M/9F, HITT n=19 11M/8F)
metadata muscle_longRNA libraries: TRAD 21x3, HITT 19x3, sex 12M/9F and 11M/8F, matching the abstract
matrix columns PHxxx_{pre,h3,h24} = 120 = the 120 muscle_longRNA GSMs

decisions.reason: Series is linked to the PMID and sample counts per arm and sex match the abstract exactly.

Metadata was subset to the 120 muscle_longRNA GSMs by prep/subset_muscle_long_metadata.py, which derives key = <PH id>_<timepoint> from the title (muscle_longRNA_PH010_w0pre -> PH010_pre), identical to the matrix column names. Exact match on key; no positional alignment.

candidates: raw_counts (confirm against provenance: normalized integers and rounded estimated counts look the same)

decisions.reason: integer_fraction 1.0, max 5.2e7, median 0; GEO data_processing: 'Long RNA count data were generated using featureCounts ... txt file containing read counts'. Features are GENCODE Ensembl gene IDs (versioned) plus LNCpedia lncRNA IDs.

selected.analysis_type: repeated-measures time course, analysed per protocol

decisions.reason: Each subject has pre, h3 and h24 muscle biopsies; the abstract's DE is 'within and between exercise protocols' at h3 and h24. Time is the factor, subject is the blocking key, protocol is a stratum (comparisons never cross it).

covariates.name: sex
covariates.disposition: absorbed by subject (constant within subject); not added

decisions.reason: Repeated biopsies from the same person: subject is a blocking term. Sex and protocol are constant within subject so they are absorbed by the subject term in the within-protocol models. All muscle long-RNA libraries were sequenced on one platform (NovaSeq 6000); no batch column is deposited.

selected.method: DESeq2 (pydeseq2 Wald), one model per protocol with all three time points

paper_route.reason: full text unavailable; abstract and GEO do not name the DE method

deviations: low-count filter (>=10 reads in >=3 samples of the fit) added for tractability on 94,946 features; not stated by the paper
between-protocol response tested by limma paired change on log2(CPM+1) (exploratory; paper's model unknown)

decisions.reason: Raw featureCounts counts support DESeq2 with subject blocking; one joint fit per protocol estimates h3 and h24 vs pre from the same model.
Abstract and GEO summary: |log2FC|>1, FDR<=0.05. Audit: FDR<0.05 without fold-change rule.
TRAD within-protocol response, one DESeq2 fit ~ subject + time on 63 samples
HITT within-protocol response, one DESeq2 fit ~ subject + time on 57 samples
between-protocol difference in the post-vs-pre change (abstract: 'between exercise protocols'); paper's model unknown, so exploratory

caveats: comparison with the paper rests on the abstract and GEO summary only; no DEG counts or gene lists from the paper are available
paper's DE method unknown; DESeq2 with subject blocking used
only skeletal-muscle long RNA analysed; EV and small/circular RNA streams not analysed

decisions.reason: Qualitative check only: abstract says TRAD elicited a generally stronger transcriptional response than HITT.
